purpose: BCG Live is mainly used to treat and prevent the return of certain types of bladder cancer that have not spread into the muscle. It is also sometimes used to prevent tuberculosis (TB) infection in people at high risk. Your doctor places it directly into your bladder through a catheter, or gives it as a skin injection for TB prevention.
how_it_works: BCG Live is actually a weakened, live form of the bacteria that causes tuberculosis in cattle. When placed inside your bladder, it stimulates your own immune system to recognize and attack cancer cells. Think of it as training your immune system to fight the cancer from the inside out.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include a burning feeling when you urinate, needing to urinate more often, blood in your urine, mild fever, fatigue, and flu-like symptoms. These usually go away within a day or two after each treatment.
warnings: Because BCG is a live bacteria, it can cause a serious infection called BCG-osis if it spreads throughout your body. Tell your doctor right away if you have a high fever, feel very ill, or develop chills after treatment. Do not use BCG if you have a weakened immune system, are pregnant, or have a urinary tract infection. Men should use a condom during sex for about 48 hours after each treatment to protect their partner. Avoid sharing a toilet with young children or immunocompromised people right after treatment.
typical_dosing: For bladder cancer, it is typically given once a week for 6 weeks, placed directly into the bladder through a thin tube called a catheter. You will hold the liquid in your bladder for about 2 hours. After that, maintenance doses may be given monthly or as your doctor recommends. For TB prevention, it is a one-time skin injection.
